summary: Defines Management Information Base objects for managing Routing Bridges, also known as TRILL Switches. Network management systems can use them to monitor and configure RBridges.

eli5.summary: A standard control panel with dials and gauges so a manager can see and adjust how these special network switches are doing.

questions: how to manage rbridges with snmp
how do i manage trill switches with snmp
subtitle: The SNMP MIB module for monitoring and configuring RBridges, also known as TRILL Switches.

tldr.problem: RBridges (TRILL Switches) needed a standard way to be managed with SNMP, covering the TRILL-specific parts that existing bridge and IS-IS MIB modules do not.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the RBRIDGE-MIB module, organized into subtrees for base, forwarding database, VLAN, ESADI, counters, snooping, distribution trees and TRILL IS-IS objects, and it reuses other MIB modules wherever it can.
tldr.outcome: Operators can manage an RBridge as a customer bridge plus TRILL-specific objects, with two notifications for Designated RBridge and topology changes.

today: RFC 6850 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2013. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 6850 describes a model for managing Routing Bridges (RBridges), also called TRILL Switches, as defined in RFC 6325. RBridges forward traffic along optimal pair-wise paths without configuration, using IS-IS routing and encapsulation. They stay compatible with earlier IEEE 802.1 customer bridges and with IPv4 and IPv6 routers and end nodes.

The management model views the device mainly as a customer bridge. Features that RBridges share with transparent bridges are managed by the matching IEEE 802.1 MIB modules, and the routing protocol by the IS-IS MIB module. The new module covers only the objects that are TRILL-specific.
sections.eli5: These special switches already have control panels for the parts they share with ordinary switches. This document adds the missing panel for the parts that are new.

sections.title: The Management Framework
sections.content:
Managed objects live in a virtual information store called the Management Information Base (MIB), which is generally accessed through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). Objects are defined with the Structure of Management Information (SMI), and this module follows SMIv2 as described in RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580.

The RFC calls the module an overall framework for managing RBridges. Where possible it refers to existing MIB definitions to maximize reuse, which puts a lot of emphasis on how it relates to other modules.
sections.eli5: The manager asks the switch questions in a common language, and every dial on the panel is described in the same standard way.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB Module
sections.content:
The objects are arranged into subtrees, each a set of related objects:

  • rbridgeBase: system and port objects for all RBridges.
  • rbridgeFdb: the forwarding database used for packet-forwarding decisions, a superset of the matching BRIDGE-MIB and Q-BRIDGE-MIB subtrees.
  • rbridgeVlan: VLANs configured on the RBridge.
  • rbridgeEsadi: objects for the optional End-Station Address Distribution Information (ESADI) protocol.
  • rbridgeCounters: statistics for monitoring and troubleshooting.
  • rbridgeSnooping: snooping of IPv4 and IPv6 multicast control frames to prune multicast traffic.
  • rbridgeDtree: distribution trees computed for multi-destination frames.
  • rbridgeTrill: TRILL IS-IS objects beyond what the ISIS-MIB offers.

Textual conventions for TRILL object types and a notifications subtree complete the module.
sections.eli5: The control panel is split into labeled sections, such as one for counters and one for forwarding tables, so each dial is easy to find.

sections.title: Relationship to Other MIB Modules
sections.content:
The IF-MIB, BRIDGE-MIB, P-BRIDGE-MIB, Q-BRIDGE-MIB, IEEE8021-BRIDGE-MIB, IEEE8021-Q-BRIDGE-MIB and ISIS-MIB modules all hold objects relevant to RBridges. Their objects are not duplicated here. Because vendors may have implemented either the IETF or the IEEE Bridge MIB modules, the RBridge MIB is designed to work with either.

The port identification elements of the IF-MIB MUST be implemented so they can be cross-referenced. The bridge modules apply when the matching functionality is implemented.

For IS-IS, RFC 4444 applies, with the TRILL constraints from RFC 6325: a single Level 1 area, the fixed area address zero, no IP address advertisement and a single protocol. Tables for IP reachability, multiple areas, levels or protocols are therefore empty. When a device runs more than one IS-IS instance, the ISIS-MIB instances are told apart by SNMPv3 contexts or SNMPv1 communities.
sections.eli5: Instead of copying dials that already exist on other panels, this one points to them, and a few of the old dials simply stay blank for these switches.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.content:
Two notifications are defined, both focused on TRILL protocol behavior. rbridgeBaseNewDrb says the sending agent has become the new Designated RBridge, and is sent soon after its election, for example when the Topology Change Timer expires.

rbridgeBaseTopologyChange is sent when any configured port moves to or from being the VLAN-x designated forwarder. It is not sent if an rbridgeBaseNewDrb notification is sent for the same transition.
sections.eli5: The switch can ring a bell for two events: when it becomes the group's leader, and when one of its ports changes jobs.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Improper manipulation of these objects may deny service to a large number of end users. Writable objects deserve care, including rbridgeBasePortTable (which can disable ports or learning), the multipath enable objects, rbridgeEsadiTable, rbridgeDtreePriority and rbridgeTrillMinMtuDesired. Readable objects can also reveal network topology.

Implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features, and those claiming SNMPv3 compliance MUST fully support authentication and privacy with the User-based Security Model and AES. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Anyone who could turn the dials could break the network, so only trusted people should get to touch them, and the messages should be protected.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The module uses one IANA-assigned object identifier recorded in the SMI Numbers registry: rbridgeMIB is { mib-2 214 }.
sections.eli5: The panel gets its own official number in a public list, so it can be told apart from every other panel.
